intro.heads_up: Quick heads-up before we dive in: Brewfest runs through October 6, so if you're after the Brewfest Barrel Bomber, Coren Direbrew is once a day and the clock is running.
rundown: a hands-on look at playing Forever on a controller
the beta's second week: a big new build, weather coming back, and another round of restarts
the name bans and Olympus marching through the beta
the fight over who Forever is actually for, and retail's answer to it
Midnight's road ahead on the 12.1.5 PTR
a heavy tuning week and the latest from the Venomous Abyss
and we'll close out the news with Brewfest and the shop, Blizzard's own Forever podcast, and Xbox's latest round of cuts

items.title: Playing Forever on a Gamepad
items.synopsis: Forever is the first WoW with real controller support, and this week's beta build gave it class flyouts, pet radials, and a pile of new gamepad options.
points: me playing the beta almost entirely on a controller: healer, rogue, and warlock so far
the radial main menu and the dynamic interact button: one press for an NPC, a herb node, whatever's in front of you
class flyouts landing on the action bar: Druid shapeshifts, Paladin auras, Warrior stances

points.text: pet control and pet spell radials only for Hunters and Warlocks: the thing I noticed before the patch notes explained it
points.sub: the pet bar also no longer replaces the bottom gamepad bar for those two classes

points: new Gamepad (Alpha) options: a compact action bar and fixed party targeting, where each d-pad direction is one party member
swap options for which side your friendly and hostile targeting live on
Edit Mode layouts finally applying with the gamepad UI on, which is how I'm moving cast bars around
the Cooldown Manager showing up off by default: five classes testable, no spell ranks yet
my setup now: one personal addon of my own, and I keep folding whatever else I need into it
questions: Would you ever raid on a controller, or is this strictly a leveling-on-the-couch thing?
If Forever launches with controller play this good, does retail have to catch up?

items.title: Forever Beta, Week Two: A New Build, Weather, and More Restarts
items.synopsis: The first full weekly beta build landed with a long class list and developer notes explaining the why, and the servers still needed another restart on Friday.
points: respecs dropping to 1 silver if you haven't changed talents recently: beta only
Druid Wrath up about 50%, heal-over-times able to crit, and Mangle renamed Primal Bite

points.text: Improved Holy Strike cut and made baseline: Blizzard saying it "felt like a talent that was required"
points.sub: one of several changes this build that came with a developer note explaining the reasoning

points: wands no longer scaling off spell damage, and Wizard Oils reverted to Classic Era values
the Hunter and wand auto-shot bug still open, with a fix promised "hopefully next week"
Jasperlode and Fargodeep mines losing their candles for being "a little more deadly than intended"
increased weather effects coming soon to the beta zones: snow and rain back in the world
Thursday's maintenance running a couple of hours, including a fix for a slow memory leak

points.text: Friday's "game is unplayable" thread and a same-day realm restart for stability fixes
points.sub: new known issue: changing your party can bounce you to a different world instance

questions: Which of these changes hold the Classic line, and which are quietly modernizing it?
Two weeks of beta restarts. Are you worried about November 4, or is this just what betas look like?

items.title: Beta Culture: Name Bans and the Olympus Army
items.synopsis: Two stories about what happens when a lot of people share one world: Blizzard pulling testers over names, and Asmongold's Olympus marching through the beta.
points: Blizzard issuing forced renames and pulling beta access for names "far outside" the Code of Conduct
dual names giving people room to be clever, and some using it to "reveal too much about themselves"
every case reviewed by the dev team, and Customer Service "cannot and will not assist with any appeals"

points.text: Tom Ellis on X: "No new standards have been set", the dual-name filter just wasn't ready yet
points.sub: 0.18% of names earned an exit from beta, and every "cheeky name" poster had a fourth character they left out

points: Asmongold reviving Olympus in the beta: reports of 30-plus full guilds and 30,000-plus members
the crowds causing lag, blocking NPCs, and making questing miserable for anyone nearby
players writing addons just to hide Olympus chat, invites, duels, and trades

points.text: the Horde's-eye view of the Olympus army marching on Undercity
points.sub: a real MMO-scale moment, whatever you think of the guy leading it

questions: No appeals on a beta ban: fair, or a precedent you don't love going into launch?
Would you want a 30,000-person guild on your ruleset at launch, or does that break the world for everyone else?

items.title: Who Is Forever For? Cornfed, and Retail's Answer
items.synopsis: A Forever world builder said convenience is the death of the journey, and the same week, Ion said retail's next expansion wants more friction too.
points: Cornfed, a self-described Forever world builder, posting from his personal account to about 2 million views
"I am making WoW Forever for the classic gamer" and the millions whose accounts lapsed over changes
a year spent relearning 20-year-old art techniques instead of the retail shortcuts he already knew

points.text: "Convenience is the death of the journey" and "if you're making a game for everyone then you're making it for no one"
points.sub: the official line from Tim Jones and Nora Mills: Forever is a third pillar, not a Classic remake or a stepping stone

points: Blizzard's site sending new players to retail and returning players to "WoW and WoW Classic"
Ion telling Windows Central The Last Titan should have a Heroic World Tier for leveling
built on Legion Remix's Heroic tier and the harder outdoor zones, no flying, tougher enemies

points.text: "We would never say 'Go play Classic if you want that.' All versions of WoW should have that."
points.sub: his words: something "like that", a goal, not a confirmed feature

questions: Is retail learning from Forever here, or trying to keep Forever players from leaving?
What does friction actually mean to you on a Tuesday night when you've only got an hour?

items.title: Midnight's Road Ahead: The 12.1.5 PTR and Kith'ix
items.synopsis: 12.1.5 is still on the PTR with no release date, and the biggest news since we last looked is Blizzard walking back its own changes.

points.text: Prot Warrior Execute walked back: Blizzard saying last week's changes "were not sufficient"
points.sub: old Execute back with a damage boost, and the real Prot rework pushed to 12.2 and 13.0

points: Devourer DH getting The Hunt and Eradicate moved out of the crowded final gate
Resto Druid's Nature's Bounty redesigned: Regrowth also healing up to three allies with Rejuvenation
Merithra's Blessing and Master the Darkness both cut to 30 seconds
a new accessibility setting, Pulse Your Health: a looping sound that gets louder as your health drops
Kith'ix raid testing on Heroic and Mythic, with testers scaled to 90
Mythic Kith'ix no longer dropping Myth 9/6 loot on the current PTR build: walking back what we said in 031
Paul Kubit and Kim Flack sitting down with Artemir on Astalor's Nemesis fight and where Talebound came from
questions: A one-boss raid without the above-cap loot. Is Kith'ix still worth a raid night for us?
Blizzard admitting a PTR change didn't work and pushing Prot to a major patch. Right call?

items.title: Tuning Week: Class Changes, Final Trinkets, and Hotfixes
items.synopsis: Blizzard went after low performers and lopsided hero talent trees, and called this the last trinket pass of Season 2.
points: the September 22 pass "mostly targeted at low performers" and hero talent gaps

points.text: Blood DK down 6% overall, with Death Strike up 15%
points.sub: announced at 25% and trimmed to 15% the day before it went live

points: Unholy Blightfall doubled to bring the build back, then a bug fix the next day added more on top
the underused hero trees pushed hard: Aldrachi Reaver, Templar, Trickster, and Mountain Thane
Disc Priest Atonement up 40% outside of raids so Disc can finally work in keys
the final raid and dungeon trinket pass for Season 2, announced a week early so you could plan loot
single-target healing trinkets buffed hard, and Season 1 holdovers like Algeth'ar Puzzle Box nerfed
hotfixes cleaning up Windwalker PvP numbers leaking into PvE, and a round of PvP snare trims
questions: Does anything here touch a spec on our roster, and is anyone swapping hero trees because of it?
Did anyone spend a vault on a trinket that just changed?

items.title: The Venomous Abyss: A Nerf Wave, and Rextroy Solos Twin Fangs
items.synopsis: Over two weeks Blizzard nerfed four bosses, buffed and then nerfed Ula'tek, and a Warrior went and soloed Twin Fangs anyway.
points: a September 15 nerf pass across Sszorak, Twin Fangs, the Coiled Altar, and Ula'tek
Mythic Putrid Membrane going from an hour to 30 seconds
Ula'tek's Mythic add waves cut: Blightscale Spawn from 13 down to 8 per wave
the Coiled Altar Soulcoiler note rewritten from "always spawns" to "increased the likelihood" after players caught it
Ula'tek quietly buffed so his tank debuff can't be outranged, per a datamined hotfix
then Stone Venom cut 40% on every difficulty with the next weekly restart

points.text: Rextroy, a Warrior, soloing Twin Fangs in the current-tier raid
points.sub: the same boss had its Mythic damage and Broodling count nerfed a week earlier

questions: Where are we on the Venomous Abyss, and did these nerfs change the plan for this reset?
A Warrior soloing a current-tier boss: class trick, or a tuning hole?

items.title: Around Azeroth: Brewfest, the Abyssal Crown, and D&D
items.synopsis: The collector's corner: Brewfest has new housing decor, the shop has Azshara, and Dungeon Masters is running a campaign in Azeroth.
points: Brewfest running through October 6: Coren Direbrew once a day for a shot at the Brewfest Barrel Bomber
Brewfest decor for your house this year: wreaths, steins, fences, banners, and crates
a Brewer's Balloon, new kilt colors, and Hunters able to tame a pink elekk during the event
October's Trading Post, Costumed Calamity, Ensemble: Thornshadow Assassin's Attire for finishing the Traveler's Log

points.text: the Abyssal Crown Collection in the shop: Azshara's Darkscale and Deepscale Raiment
points.sub: plus the Zothwing Darkseeker and Deepseeker mounts, "steeped in the dark influence of the Old Gods"

points: Dungeon Masters coming back for a third campaign, set in Azeroth and built on D&D: World of Warcraft
new episodes Wednesdays at 6:30 PM Pacific on the D&D YouTube channel
questions: Now that there's a house to put it in, is holiday decor the reason you log in for events?
After that BlizzCon one-shot. Would we actually play a WoW D&D campaign as a guild?

items.title: Blizzard's Forever Week: The Official Podcast, Toronto, and the CE Restock
items.synopsis: Blizzard launched its own Forever podcast with Aggrend, Tim Jones, and two content creators, and put more Collector's Editions on sale that won't arrive until February.
points: the WoW: Forever Podcast episode 1, Unpacking Beta Launch, Aggrend and Tim Jones with Countdown To Classic and Xaryu

points.text: episode 2 focusing on class design with the systems design team
points.sub: Aggrend on the forums asking what topics people want covered after that

points: Forever Escape Together coming to Toronto: Horde versus Alliance, ending in a Scarlet Monastery escape room
new Forever channels in the official Portal Room Discord, and a Forever Collection code giveaway
more English Collector's Editions on sale in North America, the UK, Europe, and Australia and New Zealand
restock orders shipping in February 2027: three months after the November 4 launch
a strict limit of one per household on the Gear Store
questions: Blizzard running its own podcast with streamers on it: good for the community, or a harder room for shows like ours?
Would you buy a statue that shows up three months after launch?

items.title: Xbox's Reset Continues: 268 More Cuts and Halo Moves to Activision
items.synopsis: Xbox cut another 268 roles and reorganized its studios, and Activision is now making the next Halo, while Blizzard stayed out of this round.
points: Matt Booty's "Continuing Our Reset" memo: 268 roles cut across Halo Studios, first-party studios, and Xbox management
Xbox saying it's about three-quarters of the way through the restructuring
studios folded into fewer business units, with Activision, Bethesda, and King part of the reshuffle
Activision taking over development of the next Halo
reported layoffs hitting The Coalition, World's Edge, Treyarch, and Raven
Undead Labs going independent, then announcing layoffs within hours
no Blizzard cuts reported in any of it
the lightning round: Dune: Awakening on Xbox, CONTROL Resonant, Age of Empires II's Viking Sagas, and a Gears of War: E-Day event in LA
questions: Blizzard sat this round out. Is that because Forever and Midnight are working?
What does it say that Activision is the studio Microsoft trusts with Halo?
